title: Customers Who Have Placed at Least One Order
description:
Find all customers who have placed **at least one order** using an EXISTS subquery.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`
**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `amount`, `order_date`

Return `id` and `name`. Order by `id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2), order_date DATE); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com'),(4,'Dave','dave@example.com'),(5,'Eve','eve@example.com'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,150.00,'2026-01-05'),(2,1,200.00,'2026-02-10'),(3,3,350.00,'2026-01-20'),(4,5,180.00,'2026-03-15');
solution_sql: SELECT c.id, c.name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) ORDER BY c.id

test_cases.description: 3 customers have orders: Alice(1), Carol(3), Eve(5). Bob and Dave have none.

hints: EXISTS returns TRUE if the subquery produces at least one row.
SELECT 1 inside EXISTS is conventional — the actual value doesn't matter, only whether a row exists.
explanation: For each customer, the subquery checks whether any order row has a matching customer_id. Alice (id 1) has orders 1 and 2 → EXISTS = true. Bob (id 2) has no orders → false. Carol (id 3) has order 3 → true. Dave (id 4) has none → false. Eve (id 5) has order 4 → true. Result: 3 rows.
